 Mets sign reliever Darwinzon Hernandez to three-year, $12 million deal
 The 30-year-old lefty spent the last four seasons in Japan.
 by Allison McCague Nov 20, 2026, 2:52 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The Mets and left-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernandez have agreed to a three-year, $12 million contract, according to reports .
 The 30-year-old Venezuelan last pitched in the majors four years ago, appearing in 91 games for the Red Sox from 2019 until 2022. During that time, despite flashing nasty stuff and striking out a lot of batters, he struggled mightily with walks, walking close to eight batters per nine innings and posting an ERA north of five over 85 1/3 innings for his major league career. The Red Sox designated him for assignment in January of 2023 and he had a short stint in the Orioles organization before being released in July of 2023.
 Hernandez then signed with the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks of Japan’s Nippon Professional Baseball, where he has pitched the past four season with greatly improved results. During his time in NPB, he has put up a 2.46 ERA in 131 2/3 innings and struck out close to a third of the batters he has faced, owning the second-highest strikeout rate in NPB among relievers since 2024 . Most importantly, he lowered his walk rate to 8%, which is less than half of what it was during his time in Boston. Hernandez features a four-seam fastball, a slider, and a curveball.
 Alex Speier of The Boston Globe recently reported that Hernandez was looking to return to MLB this season and the Mets, in need of arms, are giving him that chance. The deal , which is still pending a physical, includes a $500,000 signing bonus, a $4 million salary for 2027, and a $3.75 million salary in each of the two subsequent years.
